mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-13.7, -13.4, -12.1, -10.9), indicating a self-reinforcing recovery in discretionary mobility. This momentum is expected to continue, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days versus the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically over the last three observed weeks
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite the prior three-week uptrend, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility recovering past a threshold signals renewed commuting and errand trips that mechanically funnel people past retail storefronts, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -6 points week-on-week after being below -8 for two consecutive prior weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -9.4 to -5.3 over two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -6, the threshold trigger mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compounds to increase total daytime out-of-home activity, producing a stronger and faster lift in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, acting over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise week-on-week simultaneously for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -9.3 to -3.7 and TRANSIT from -9.4 to -5.3 over the same two-week window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's four-week increase is no larger than what single-series models (WORKPLACES-only or TRANSIT-only) would predict, the interaction effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated and rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (31.6 to 37.6 over four weeks) reflects a precautionary stockpiling behavior pattern associated with anticipated disruption, which substitutes for and suppresses discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose each of the last three weeks to 37.6
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite continued elevation and growth in GROCERY_PHARM, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The rebound in PARKS mobility from -17.0 to -14.6 in the most recent week reflects a seasonal shift toward outdoor activity that is typically accompanied by nearby retail and dining visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -17.0 to -14.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a PARKS rebound, the seasonal co-movement mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining persistently elevated near +6 to +7 points signals continued stay-at-home policy or compliance behavior; if RESIDENTIAL stays above a sustained threshold, retail recovery stalls because underlying restrictions on gatherings and venue capacity remain binding.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +6 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed between 6.0 and 7.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above +6, the policy-binding mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM growth outpaces RETAIL_REC growth week-on-week, households are reallocating a fixed mobility budget toward essential errands at the expense of discretionary shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to underperform over the next four weeks relative to its own trend.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change exceeds RETAIL_REC week-on-week change by more than 3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 2.5 points while RETAIL_REC rose 1.2 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's four-week mean rises despite GROCERY_PHARM consistently outpacing it week-on-week, the reallocation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of WORKPLACES above -5 points indicates a critical mass of workers returning to in-person work, which immediately increases nearby lunchtime and after-work retail visits within one week of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses above -5 points after being below -5 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -9.3 to -4.6 to -3.7, crossing above -5 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following WORKPLACES crossing above -5, the crossing-trigger mechanism is rejected.
